title: Power Automate: configure Flow checker rules and notifications for desktop flows in the admin portal
summary: Hold: the claim that Microsoft Learn publishes no licensing requirement for rule configuration overlooks the published licensing requirements of its Managed Environments prerequisite. Notification-specific licensing and notification controls remain undocumented; those gaps are correctly distinguished from the documented rule settings.

Known limitations

claims.where: Cost and licensing: first sentence; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn names no licence for Flow checker rule configuration, leaving admin time as the only known cost.
claims.quote: When you activate managed environments in an environment, all active usage requires one of these standalone licenses or pay-as-you-go meters.
claims.fix: Replace the broad no-licence assertion with: 'The documented rule configuration requires Managed Environments. Microsoft publishes licensing requirements for that tier: all active usage requires a qualifying standalone licence or meter. Notification-specific licensing or charges are not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-licensing. In licensing.notes retain unknown only for notification-specific licensing and state that the published Managed Environments requirements apply to the documented controls. Narrow the cost rationale to: 'Low. Admin time is the known incremental cost for environments already entitled to Managed Environments; notification-specific charges are not yet published.'
